Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
50-year-old woman with 5-day history of dry, persistent cough and runny nose; likely viral upper respiratory tract infection.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Dry, continuous cough and rhinorrhea for ~5–6 days; cough disturbs sleep.  
• Associated symptoms: Fatigue, chills/subjective fever, diffuse myalgia (arms and legs), initial brief diarrhea (resolved). No sputum, chest pain, significant dyspnea (only during coughing), sore throat only from irritation, ear symptoms, nausea/vomiting, urinary symptoms, or rash.  
• Pertinent negatives: No sputum production, no chest pain, no sustained dyspnea, no nausea/vomiting.  
• Past medical history: Type 2 diabetes; hypertension.  
• Medications: Metformin – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
  Lisinopril – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• Allergies: Denies medication allergies.  
• Social: Lives with partner; IT developer; former smoker (quit 6 months ago); drinks wine 2–3 glasses on ~3 evenings/week.

Examination:
• Vitals: Not documented.  
• Physical findings: Not documented.

Impression:
Likely viral upper respiratory tract infection (self-limiting).

Plan:
• Conservative care: Rest, maintain hydration, regular paracetamol as needed.  
• Off-work advice: Consider 1–2 days off work to reduce spread and allow recovery; reassess work early next week.  
• Safety-netting: Return within 2–3 days if no improvement or sooner if worsening cough, new/worsening fever, or increased breathlessness; may consider antibiotics on re-evaluation.  
• Lifestyle: Advised to reduce alcohol gradually (goal ≤2 glasses/week, then taper further) to support BP/diabetes control.

Quality checks:
● Missing typical elements: Objective vitals, physical examination, allergy verification beyond medications, current blood pressure/diabetes control data, medication dosages.  
● Conflicts: None noted.  
● Transcript quality: Clear; no major inaudible sections.
